PoCs live in ${POCS} (npm workspace, deps already installed — do NOT npm install / add deps). READ FIRST: ${POCS}/CONTRACT.md (ports, shared lib/db.ts + lib/llm.ts, SQLite tables, hand-off URLs, code+UI rules). Original product brief (Korean): ${ROOT}/docs/SUPER_PLANER_CONTEXT.md. Code style: follow ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md (full level) — smallest complete code, no speculative abstraction, but never cut validation/security/error handling/accessibility. UI: follow ${POCS}/DESIGN.md and ${POCS}/shared/tokens.css (hallmark Floor in ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/hallmark/SKILL.md). Plain CSS (CSS modules or globals.css) using the tokens — no Tailwind, no UI kits. All UI copy in Korean, plain and specific. No emoji icons; use inline SVG icons when needed. This environment runs inside Claude Code: the shell env has CLAUDECODE set; lib/llm.ts already strips it for the claude CLI. Use LLM_PROVIDER=mock for all routine testing. If you start a server, use the app's own port, run it in the background, and KILL it before you finish (lsof -ti tcp: | xargs kill). ` const SPECS = { step1: ` APP: ${POCS}/step1 (port 3101) — "바이브 프롬프트 → 소크라테스식 질문" Brief: input = text prompt; output = question workflow (질문 워크플로우), game title (가제), short description. First prompt → { question → answer (choice + free text mixed) } × N → result. Method references (read them): ouroboros socratic interviewer ${ROOT}/docs/references/ouroboros-socratic-interviewer.md and ${ROOT}/docs/references/ouroboros-interview-skill.md (more in ${REFS}/Q00_ouroboros, e.g. src/ouroboros/bigbang/interview.py, interview_calibration.py, docs/auto-interview-convergence-contract.md — skim for ambiguity scoring/tracks/closure). ELI5: ${ROOT}/docs/references/eli5-skill.md. Required behaviour: 1. Home: one large textarea ("어떤 게임을 만들고 싶나요? 대충 적어도 돼요" style), a few example prompts to click, start button. Creates a step1_sessions row. 2. Interview engine (lib/interview.ts), ouroboros-style: - At start infer ambiguity TRACKS from the prompt (e.g. 핵심 재미/장르, 플레이어 역할, 코어 루프, 이기고 지는 조건, 플랫폼·한 판 길이, 분위기·아트, 누가 할 게임인지, 다른 게임과 다른 점). Keep a per-track ambiguity score 0..1 and an overall ambiguity. - Each turn: pick the most ambiguous track (breadth control: after 2 consecutive turns on one track, zoom out to another), ask ONE Socratic question that builds on previous answers. Rules from ouroboros: 1–2 sentences, always ends with a question, no preamble ("좋은 질문이에요" banned), target the biggest ambiguity, ontological where useful ("이 게임은 결국 무엇을 하는 게임인가요?"). - ELI5 for ages 15–20 (Age 15 + Senior High/College styles): casual but not cringey, game/phone/social analogies, one idea per sentence, any jargon defined inline (e.g. "코어 루프(게임에서 계속 반복하는 행동)"). Each question has a one-line 'hint' analogy. - Answers mix selection and input: 3–5 options (single or multi select — add a 'multi' column if needed; owners may add columns) PLUS a free-text field, both usable together; plus a "잘 모르겠어요, 추천해 줘" choice. - Stop: overall ambiguity ≤ 0.2, or 8 questions max, or the user presses "여기까지로 정리하기". Before generating the result run ouroboros' Restate gate: show the decisions as a short summary and ask "이대로 정리할까요?" (confirm / one more question). - Provider: completeJSON() from lib/llm.ts with a system prompt combining the socratic + ELI5 rules, returning strict JSON {track, question, hint, options, multi, allow_free, ambiguity:{[track]:number}, done}. Deterministic fallback (mock): a question bank per track whose wording and options adapt to keywords from the prompt and previous answers, with deterministic ambiguity updates (answered track drops). The mock must feel like a real interview. 3. Q/A UX: one current question card at a time with smooth step transition; answered turns appear as a vertical "질문 워크플로우" (connected nodes: Q → A) beside/above it; ambiguity ledger visible (track list with 명확/애매 state and the overall number). Keyboard usable (Enter submits, number keys pick options is a nice-to-have). 4. Result screen in ELI5 format: 게임 이름(가제), 한 줄 설명, "이게 뭐냐면"(what, one sentence), "비유하자면"(analogy), "조금 더 자세히"(details bullets), "그래서 왜 재밌냐면"(so what), decisions list per track, and the full 질문 워크플로우. Generated by completeJSON with ELI5 rules + deterministic fallback. Stored in step1_results. Buttons: "워크플로우로 열기" → http://localhost:3102/?from=step1:, "새로 시작". 5. Session list (recent sessions) so the human can revisit. Sessions persist across reloads (state in SQLite, URL /s/). 6. Self-check: lib/interview.test.* covering mock track selection, breadth control, stop condition. `, 'workflow-view': ` APP: ${POCS}/workflow-view (port 3102) — "n8n 같은 워크플로우 시각화" Brief: full-canvas n8n-like visualizer of cards + connectors. Card = '타이틀', '설명', expand/collapse button, 동결(complete)/취소(undo) buttons, status (진행중/동결/취소). Expanded card shows an agent chat session. URLs in agent answers render previews as a gallery (slide or grid). Use @xyflow/react 12 (installed). Required behaviour: 1. Full-viewport canvas: dotted background, pan/zoom, Controls, MiniMap, fit view. Nodes draggable (positions persisted to wf_cards on drag stop), edges as smooth/bezier connectors with visible handles; user can connect two cards by dragging handle → handle (persist to wf_edges) and delete an edge. Toolbar: workflow title + selector (all wf_workflows), "카드 추가" (creates an active card near viewport center with title/description inputs), "기획서 만들기" link → http://localhost:3103/?workflow= (enabled only when ≥1 frozen card), provider label. 2. Card (custom node): title, description, status text (진행중/동결/취소) styled distinctly (cancelled dimmed + struck title, frozen with a locked look), expand/collapse button, 동결 button, 취소 button. Semantics: 동결 = complete: active → frozen, writes 'decision' (summary of the chat via completeJSON, deterministic fallback = last agent message condensed), chat becomes read-only, decision shown at top. 취소 = undo: on an active card → cancelled; on a frozen or cancelled card the same button reads "되돌리기" and returns it to active. Buttons need nodrag/nopan classes so they work on the canvas. 3. Expanded card = agent chat session (larger node, e.g. ~440×560, scrollable messages with class 'nowheel'): agent messages left with agent icon/name, user messages right, timestamps, simple markdown-ish rendering (paragraphs, lists, bold, links). Input at bottom; sending stores a user message and gets an agent reply via completeJSON (the agent role: a game-planning sub-agent for that card's topic that answers with concrete suggestions and 1–4 reference URLs: images and pages). Deterministic fallback reply includes reference URLs too. 4. URL previews: extract http(s) URLs from agent messages (lib/urls.ts, with test). Under the message render a gallery with a toggle 슬라이드 / 격자: slide = horizontal scroll-snap carousel with prev/next buttons + position text; grid = 2-col grid. Image URLs (by extension or picsum.photos/images.unsplash.com hosts) render as directly (lazy, with alt, fallback on error). Page URLs call GET /api/preview?url= which fetches og:title/og:description/og:image/site name server-side and caches in wf_link_previews. SSRF guard is mandatory: only http/https, resolve DNS and reject loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/metadata IPs (v4+v6), manual redirect following (max 3) re-checking each hop, 5s timeout, cap body at ~1MB, only parse text/html. Failure → simple card with host + URL. Clicking an image opens a larger lightbox (Esc closes, focus managed). 5. Seed (when no workflows exist): one sample game workflow (Korean, e.g. a cozy roguelike) with 6–7 cards in a left→right DAG (컨셉, 코어 루프, 캐릭터, 레벨 디자인, 아트 방향, 수익 모델 …), mixed statuses, each with 2–4 seeded chat messages; agent messages include real URLs: images from https://picsum.photos/id//800/500 and local sample SVG concept images you create in public/samples/*.svg (referenced as absolute http://localhost:3102/samples/...; treat as image by extension, never server-fetched), plus page URLs like https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roguelike and https://github.com/xyflow/xyflow. 6. Import: /?from=step1: creates (idempotently, source='step1:') a workflow from step1 tables if they exist: a concept card (from step1_results) then one frozen card per answered turn (title = track/question short, description = question, decision = answer, messages = the Q as agent + answer as user), chained by edges, laid out left→right in rows. Unknown id → friendly message. 7. API: route handlers under app/api (runtime nodejs). Validate inputs. Self-checks: lib/urls.test.* and an SSRF-guard test (private IPs rejected). `, 'plan-doc': ` APP: ${POCS}/plan-doc (port 3103) — "기획서 생성 도구" Brief: input = vibe-generated agent decision documents + vibe-generated example images; output = a Markdown plan document shown in a Markdown Preview, with images rendered inside the Markdown. Use react-markdown 10 + remark-gfm 4 (installed). Required behaviour: 1. Layout: left = inputs, right = document. Inputs panel: (a) 결정 문서 list with checkboxes (title + body preview), add/edit/delete a decision (title + markdown body); (b) 이미지 예시 gallery with checkboxes + caption, add by upload (png/jpg/webp/gif only — validate MIME by magic bytes, ≤5MB, NO svg uploads; stored under ${POCS}/.data/uploads and served via GET /api/images/) or by https URL. Seed sample inputs when empty: 5 decision docs for a sample game (Korean, consistent with a cozy roguelike) and 4 sample concept images you create as SVG in public/samples/*.svg (character, level, UI mock, mood) — make them look like simple flat concept sketches, not placeholders. 2. "기획서 만들기" → POST /api/generate with selected decision + image ids → completeJSON with a planner system prompt producing Markdown; deterministic fallback lib/assemble.ts builds the doc from inputs. Required doc structure: # <게임 가제> 기획서, 개요 (한 줄 소개, 장르, 플랫폼, 타깃), 핵심 재미, 코어 루프 (numbered), 주요 시스템, 아트·분위기 (embed selected images as ![caption](url) with captions), 결정 로그 (GFM table: 항목 | 결정 | 출처), 열린 질문/리스크, 다음 단계. Every selected image must appear in the Markdown. Save to plan_docs. 3. Document panel: tabs 미리보기 / 마크다운 / 나란히; the markdown tab is an editable textarea with live preview; edits saved (debounced or explicit 저장). Preview styled as a readable document (good typography for headings, tables, lists, blockquotes, code, images max-width 100% with figure-like caption from alt). Buttons: .md 다운로드, 마크다운 복사. Saved docs list to reopen previous versions. 4. Imports: /?workflow= imports (idempotent, source='wf:') every frozen wf_cards row (title + decision → decision input) and every image URL found in that card's wf_messages (image extensions or picsum.photos) → image input, if the wf_* tables exist, then preselects them. Also a small "Step1 결과 가져오기" picker listing step1_results (if table exists) → one decision input with the ELI5 concept (source='step1:'). 5. Security: react-markdown default (no raw HTML). Validate API input. Self-check lib/assemble.test.* (all sections present, every image embedded, table escapes '|'). `, } const VERIFY_SCHEMA = { type: 'object', properties: { passed: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true only if no blocker/major issues remain' }, issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor'] }, area: { type: 'string' }, description: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, }, required: ['severity', 'description'] } }, checks_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, }, required: ['passed', 'issues', 'checks_run'], } // ---------- Design ---------- phase('Design') await agent(`${COMMON} You are the design lead. Produce the shared visual system for three Korean product-tool PoCs of "Super Planer" (게임 기획자를 위한 워크플로우 시각화 서비스): step1 (Socratic Q/A interview), workflow-view (n8n-like canvas with chat cards), plan-doc (markdown plan document editor/preview). Use the hallmark skill as your method: read ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/hallmark/SKILL.md, references/design-md.md, references/gates.md, references/fonts.md, and pick a theme from references/themes/ (look at the .md files; you may view the .jpg previews) that suits a calm, precise planning tool. Brand constraints: primary indigo #4F46E5 (logo symbol), ink #151923, logo ${ROOT}/assets/super-planer-logo.svg / super-planer-icon.svg. Do not ask the user anything; audience = game planners/designers, use = daily work tool, tone = calm, precise, slightly playful. Write: 1. ${POCS}/DESIGN.md (hallmark design.md format): direction, tokens table, type scale, spacing, radii, elevation, motion (durations/easings, reduced-motion), component recipes needed by all three apps: app header (logo + 3 PoC links: 질문하기 :3101 / 워크플로우 :3102 / 기획서 :3103, current marked), buttons (primary/secondary/ghost/danger), text inputs/textarea, chips/options (selectable), panel, status labels (진행중/동결/취소 without decorative dots), chat bubbles, gallery, tabs, markdown document typography. Give the exact CSS class names + minimal markup for each recipe so three independent builders produce consistent UIs. 2. ${POCS}/shared/tokens.css: the hallmark stamp + critique line first, then :root tokens (colors, fonts with system/Korean-friendly stacks — Pretendard is NOT installed; if you want a webfont, load from Google Fonts via @import in tokens.css e.g. 'IBM Plex Sans KR' or 'Noto Sans KR'), light + dark (prefers-color-scheme), plus the base element styles and the shared component classes from DESIGN.md (header, buttons, inputs, chips, status labels, tabs, panel). Respect every Floor rule (focus-visible, no transition: all, reduced-motion, overflow-x: clip on html/body, tokens only). 3. Run: node ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs ${POCS}/shared --scope app — fix FAILs. Return a short summary of the direction and the class names.`, { label: 'design-system', phase: 'Design' }) // ---------- Build → Verify/Fix ---------- const APPS = ['step1', 'workflow-view', 'plan-doc'] const buildPrompt = (app) => `${COMMON} You are the builder for ONE app. ${SPECS[app]} Do it completely: pages, route handlers, lib/schema.ts (own tables only, per CONTRACT), seed, styles (app/globals.css starting with @import "../../shared/tokens.css"; use DESIGN.md class recipes), shared header, self-check tests. Copy logo SVGs from ${ROOT}/assets into public/. Work only inside ${POCS}/${app} (never edit other apps, shared/, CONTRACT.md or DESIGN.md — if you need a shared change, report it). Before finishing: (1) cd ${POCS}/${app} && npx tsc --noEmit; (2) npx next build; (3) run your self-check tests; (4) start the app with LLM_PROVIDER=mock on its port, exercise the main flow end-to-end with curl (pages return 200, APIs do the right thing, DB rows written), then kill the server; (5) node ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs ${POCS}/shared ${POCS}/${app}/app --scope app and fix FAILs. ${app === 'step1' ? 'Also make ONE real call with LLM_PROVIDER=claude-cli (e.g. a small script or a curl to your API with the server started with that env) to confirm the prompt yields parseable JSON in Korean ELI5 style; tune the prompt if not. It may take ~30s.' : ''} Return: files created, how to use, known limits.` const verifyPrompt = (app, round) => `${COMMON} You are an independent, skeptical verifier (round ${round}) for ${POCS}/${app}. Do NOT edit any files. ${SPECS[app]} Check everything with evidence: - npx tsc --noEmit and npx next build in ${POCS}/${app} succeed. - Self-check tests exist and pass. - Start with LLM_PROVIDER=mock on its port (background), then drive the whole flow with curl/node fetch: every required behaviour in the spec above — e.g. full interview to result for step1; card CRUD, status transitions (동결/취소/되돌리기), chat send, preview API incl. SSRF rejection of http://127.0.0.1, http://169.254.169.254, http://[::1] for workflow-view; inputs, upload validation (reject svg/oversize), generate, every selected image embedded, save/reopen for plan-doc. Inspect the SQLite rows (node -e with node:sqlite on ${POCS}/.data/super-planer.db) and confirm they match CONTRACT.md columns. - Read the UI code: does it actually implement every UI requirement (e.g. expand shows chat, gallery slide/grid toggle, Q/A shows mixed choice+free text, markdown preview shows images, tabs, Restate gate)? Missing or stubbed = major. - Security/robustness at trust boundaries; crashes on bad input = major. - sloplint: node ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs ${POCS}/shared ${POCS}/${app}/app --scope app — any FAIL = minor (major if many). Kill the server when done. Be concrete: each issue with file:line or the failing command output. passed=true only when no blocker/major issues.` const fixPrompt = (app, issues) => `${COMMON} You are fixing ${POCS}/${app} after an independent verification. ${SPECS[app]} Fix every blocker and major issue, and minor ones when cheap. Work only inside ${POCS}/${app}. Issues: ${JSON.stringify(issues, null, 2)} After fixing, re-run tsc, next build, the self-checks and the relevant curl flows (LLM_PROVIDER=mock, kill the server after). Return what you changed.` const results = await pipeline( APPS, (app) => agent(buildPrompt(app), { label: `build:${app}`, phase: 'Build' }), async (_built, app) => { let v = null for (let round = 1; round <= 3; round++) { v = await agent(verifyPrompt(app, round), { label: `verify:${app}:r${round}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERIFY_SCHEMA }) if (!v) break const serious = v.issues.filter((i) => i.severity !== 'minor') log(`${app} round ${round}: ${serious.length} blocker/major, ${v.issues.length - serious.length} minor`) if (v.passed && serious.length === 0) { if (v.issues.length) await agent(fixPrompt(app, v.issues), { label: `polish:${app}`, phase: 'Verify' }) break } if (round === 3) { log(`${app}: still has issues after 3 rounds`); break } await agent(fixPrompt(app, v.issues), { label: `fix:${app}:r${round}`, phase: 'Verify' }) } return { app, verdict: v } }, ) // ---------- Integrate (needs all three apps) ---------- phase('Integrate') const integration = await agent(`${COMMON} You own cross-app integration. All three apps are built. Test the full hand-off chain with LLM_PROVIDER=mock, starting all three servers (cd ${POCS}; start each with LLM_PROVIDER=mock npm run dev -w in background on 3101/3102/3103): 1. step1: create a session via its API, answer questions until done, confirm through the Restate gate, generate the result. 2. Open http://localhost:3102/?from=step1: — confirm a workflow is created from that session (cards, frozen answered turns with decision, edges), idempotent on reload. 3. In that workflow, send a chat message on an active card, freeze a card, then open http://localhost:3103/?workflow= — confirm decisions + image URLs are imported (idempotent) and a generated doc contains them and embeds the images. 4. Check the shared header links on all three apps and that every hand-off link/button points at the right URL. 5. Also check the fresh-DB path: move ${POCS}/.data aside (rename to .data.bak-int), start apps, confirm each app seeds itself and works standalone, then restore the original .data. Fix any integration bug in whichever app owns it (smallest change; keep CONTRACT.md the source of truth, update it only if the contract was ambiguous). Re-run tsc for apps you edit. Kill all servers when done. Return: chain result per step (pass/fail + evidence) and changes made.`, { label: 'integration', phase: 'Integrate' }) // ---------- Visual QA ---------- phase('Visual QA') const visual = await agent(`${COMMON} You are the visual QA + hallmark slop-removal pass. Start all three apps (LLM_PROVIDER=mock, ports 3101/3102/3103, background). Use the chrome-devtools MCP tools (load them via ToolSearch, e.g. "select:mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page,mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page,mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot,mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot,mcp__chrome-devtools__click,mcp__chrome-devtools__fill,mcp__chrome-devtools__resize_page,mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages,mcp__chrome-devtools__press_key,mcp__chrome-devtools__type_text") to open each app at 1440×900 and 390×844, walk the main flows (step1: prompt → 2-3 answers → stop → restate → result; workflow-view: expand a card, see chat + gallery in both slide and grid modes, freeze/undo; plan-doc: generate a doc, see images in preview, switch tabs), take screenshots, and check console errors. Judge against ${POCS}/DESIGN.md and the hallmark Floor + review-finish (${ROOT}/.claude/skills/hallmark/references/review-finish.md): consistency across the three apps, hierarchy, spacing rhythm, contrast, focus states, overflow at mobile width, no generic AI-slop patterns (gradient blobs, card-in-card, eyebrow labels, emoji icons, dot status, invented metrics, filler copy). Fix what you find directly in the app code (smallest changes, tokens only). Re-screenshot after fixes to confirm. Run sloplint for each app at the end. Close pages and kill servers when done. Return: per app what you fixed and anything left.`, { label: 'visual-qa', phase: 'Visual QA' }) // ---------- Audit ---------- phase('Audit') const audit = await agent(`${COMMON} You are the completeness critic. Compare the implementation in ${POCS} line-by-line against EVERY bullet of the brief in ${ROOT}/docs/SUPER_PLANER_CONTEXT.md (PoC section 1, 2, 3 and the top-level bullets) and CONTRACT.md. For each bullet: implemented? where (file:line)? how a human verifies it in the browser. Run tsc + self-check tests for all three apps one final time (no servers needed unless to confirm a doubt; kill any you start). If you find a gap that is small, fix it. Then write ${POCS}/README.md (Korean): what each PoC is, how to run (npm run dev in pocs → URLs; LLM provider options: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / local claude CLI / LLM_PROVIDER=mock; DB location; reset by deleting pocs/.data), and a HIL checklist per PoC (checkbox list of concrete things the human should try and what they should see), plus known limits. Return JSON-ish text: per-bullet status table, gaps fixed, gaps remaining.`, { label: 'spec-audit', phase: 'Audit' }) return { results, integration, visual, audit }

issues.description: parseQuestion only checks that the question ends with '?' and has at least 2 options. It does not enforce the ouroboros rules of one question, 1-2 sentences and no preamble. With a real LLM, a reply such as '좋은 질문이에요! 뭘 할까요? 그리고 왜요?' would be shown as is. The rules exist only in the system prompt.
issues.evidence: step1/lib/interview.ts:429 `const ok = TRACK_KEYS.includes(track) && track !== blocked && /[?？]$/.test(question) && options.length >= 2;` Fuzz run: parseQuestion({track:'fun',question:'좋은 질문이에요! 뭘 할까요? 그리고 왜요?',options:['a','b']}) returns a valid q.

issues.description: The mock text puts a fixed '를' after a quoted prompt instead of using the josa() helper. A prompt ending in a final consonant then reads wrongly, e.g. '“고양이가 … 느긋한 게임”를'. This shows when the user wraps up before loop or fun is answered.
issues.evidence: step1/lib/interview.ts:334 goalLine `“${short(prompt, 60)}”를 바탕으로`; :372 `“${short(prompt, 40)}”를 직접 해 보는`. Fuzz output: one_liner '“테스트 게임”를 바탕으로 한 게임이에요.'

issues.description: An answer of '잘 모르겠어요, 추천해 줘' is stored as that raw text in step1_turns.answer.choices. Step1 resolves it to the first option plus '(추천)' only for display (decisionOf). workflow-view's importer joins choices as is, so the imported frozen card's decision reads '잘 모르겠어요, 추천해 줘' instead of the recommended option.

toggle() updates the expanded state in the UI before the server answers. If the PATCH fails, the change is not undone, so the UI and the DB disagree until reload. Card positions are saved after a 250ms delay, so a page change right after a drag can lose the new position.

Testing was done through the APIs and server-rendered HTML only: the browser tool was already in use by another session, so I couldn't check the client-rendered parts (canvas drawing, markdown preview) by eye.

**1. step1: pass.**
- `POST /api/sessions` created session `17a6f69316`. I answered 7 questions (tracks fun, loop, win, unique, mood, audience, platform) with a mix of picked options and typed text; one typed answer included `https://picsum.photos/id/237/600/400`.

**2. workflow-view import: pass.**

**3. Edit in workflow-view, then plan-doc: pass.**
- Every imported card starts frozen, so there was no active card to chat on. Chat on a frozen card is rejected with 409, as designed. I undid "분위기와 그림체" back to active, sent a message containing an image link (got a mock reply with a picsum link, 201), then froze it (decision written, provider mock).
- I also added a new active card with an edge and chatted on it.

- Importing into plan-doc twice gave 11 ids both times: 8 decisions and 3 images (`picsum 237`, `1043`, `180`). The total stayed at 36, so the re-import added nothing. The new card wasn't imported because it isn't frozen.
- The generated doc "우주 고양이 퍼즐" (mock) contains all 8 decisions in the 결정 로그 table and embeds all 3 images as `![..](https://picsum.photos/...)`.

**4. Header and hand-off links: pass.**
- All three apps show the same header: logo, then 질문하기 / 워크플로우 / 기획서 linking to `http://localhost:3101/`, `3102/` and `3103/`, with `aria-current="page"` on the current app and an "LLM: mock" label.

Link preview works for a Wikipedia page and blocks `127.0.0.1:3101` with "port 3101 not allowed".

Things worth knowing:
- **Re-freezing doesn't update plan-doc:** if a card is undone and frozen again with a new decision, plan-doc keeps the copy it already imported. This is on purpose (so an edited copy in plan-doc isn't overwritten), and `CONTRACT.md` only says "idempotent".
- **Imported cards are all frozen:** anyone testing chat on a step1 workflow has to undo a card first or add a new one.
- **Typed answers get cut off:** step1 shortens a long typed answer inside the one-liner ("…밀어 옮겨요 htt…"). That's a text quirk, not a hand-off problem.

Instead I drove a separate headless Chrome with the puppeteer-core that comes with that MCP, using its own profile in the scratchpad. Also, all three dev servers were stopped by a SIGTERM partway through, probably another agent clearing the same ports. I restarted them and finished.

- **step1:** prompt, three answers, "여기까지로 정리하기", the restate step, then the result. No console errors and no horizontal overflow at 390px.
- **workflow-view:** expanding a card, the gallery in slide and grid views, the image lightbox, freeze/undo, and the cancelled state. The only console error was a missing `/favicon.ico`, now fixed.
- **plan-doc:** generating a doc and switching all three tabs, including with arrow keys. All 9 preview images load once you scroll to them, including the SVG samples and the image from port 3102. No console errors and no page overflow at 390px.
- **Focus rings:** visible on chips, buttons, tabs and workflow cards.

**step1 fixes**
- The score in the "애매한 부분" panel sat alone on a line under each bar. It's now on the label row ("명확 0.15") with the bar below (`step1/app/globals.css`).
- On phones the question card was squeezed into a narrow column. I tightened its padding and the indent beside it below 40rem.
- The Next.js dev badge covered a "최근 세션" link on mobile, so I turned it off (`step1/next.config.ts`).

**workflow-view fixes**
- Bullet lists inside agent messages showed a broken half-circle marker. They now use normal discs and numbers in the muted colour (`pocs/shared/tokens.css`, chat section).
- Added the favicon, which fixed the 404. The tab title now matches the other apps: "워크플로우 - Super Planer" (`workflow-view/app/layout.tsx`).
- The dev badge covered the canvas "전체 보기" button, so I turned it off (`workflow-view/next.config.ts`).

**plan-doc fixes**
- The dev badge covered the sticky "기획서 만들기" button on mobile, so I turned it off (`plan-doc/next.config.ts`).

- **State my walkthrough changed:** I put "레벨 디자인" back to 진행중 and collapsed the concept card. The two new step1 sessions and one generated plan doc are still there.
